text: Hello — this is Sarah. I'm new to the department this term and I haven't read the department handbook yet. Could you send me a copy, or point me to where I can find it? I'd like to know the rules I should follow when I'm asked to put things in my schedule (lectures, seminars, university meetings). Thanks!

Welcome, Sarah — glad to have you. I'm the department office. There's no separate public copy I can hand out, but here are the rules that matter for your schedule; the same ones apply to everyone in the department:

**Working hours** Monday–Friday, 09:00–17:00.

**Official events are fixed.** Lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committee and department meetings only change when the department office announces it in writing to those concerned. "Someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — ask the office before you rely on it.

**Your calendar is the record of your commitments.** You don't delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one instead. And a meeting is booked only when every participant has it on their calendar.

**If someone says you agreed to something or told them something and you don't remember it,** check before acting on it: ask them for details and check the facts with the office.

**For students:** attend your lectures and sections — a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it's cancelled. Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

**Privacy:** don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent, and neither do I.

**Complaints** (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they're handled there and don't change these scheduling rules.

If you tell me your courses, I can tell you the official times for next week — just ask.

Thank you, that's very helpful — I've noted the rules.

Since I'm new, I'm not sure yet which courses I'm down for. My advisor is Professor Alvarez (CSE455). Could you send me the official times for next week for CSE455, and tell me whether I'm enrolled in or assigned to CSE444 or CSE452? Then I can check my calendar against the official record.

As for CSE444 and CSE452: I keep the department's official teaching schedule, not individual enrolment or assignment records, so I can't tell you whether you're enrolled in or assigned to a course. Your adviser or the registrar's student records can confirm that. What I can do is give you the official times for CSE444 and CSE452 as well, if that helps you check your calendar — just say the word.
